issues.legal_issue: The market value of acquired land cannot be determined by extrapolating backward from the value of land acquired substantially later.
material_facts: The land was acquired as a large tract of undeveloped agricultural land for residential development.
The landowners relied on compensation rates determined for nearby land acquired about ten years later and proposed reducing those rates by ten percent annually to estimate the earlier value.
The landowners had not produced sale deeds showing the market value of comparable land at or before the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The later-acquired land and a retrospective annual reduction could not be used to determine the market value on the acquisition date; the proposed method was misconceived and unsupported by the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, market value is assessed by reference to the market rate of similarly situated land prevailing on the acquisition date or before it. Escalation may be appropriate in some cases when supported by sale deeds for comparable land, but the Court held that the proposed retrospective calculation from land acquired later was not a method provided by the Act. The Court also relied on the established principles for valuing undeveloped land and making development deductions in Brig. Sahib Singh Kalha v. Amritsar Improvement Trust, Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Kasturi v. State of Haryana, Lal Chand v. Union of India, A.P. Housing Board v. K. Manohar Reddy, Special Land Acquisition Officer v. M.K. Rafiq Saheb, and Chandrashekar v. Land Acquisition Officer.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired by the government.
predicates.later_acquired_comparable_used: A party relies on land acquired after the subject land to support the subject land’s earlier market value.
predicates.retrospective_price_reduction_proposed: A party proposes reducing the later land value year by year to estimate the earlier value.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal relies on later-acquired land and a proposed backward price reduction, that later value cannot establish the subject land’s earlier market value.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation award must reflect the market value the deciding court itself has found on the evidence and applicable valuation factors.
material_facts: The land was a large tract of undeveloped agricultural land acquired for residential development.
The landowners presented oral evidence about the land’s location, access, surroundings, and development potential, but no sale deeds.
The High Court considered the land’s potential and the rate fixed by courts for adjacent land acquired at the same time, and stated that the market value was sixty-three rupees per square yard.
Despite that finding, the High Court awarded compensation at fifty rupees per square yard.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had no justification for awarding less than the market value it had found; the Supreme Court fixed compensation at sixty-three rupees per square yard, with the statutory benefits payable under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 requires assessment of fair market value as of the acquisition date. The Court considered the land’s location, potential, surroundings, nearby land values, undeveloped condition, and development costs, while recognizing that valuation requires assessment of the evidence rather than an exact formula. It applied the principles on development deductions in Brig. Sahib Singh Kalha v. Amritsar Improvement Trust, Chimanlal Hargovinddas v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Kasturi v. State of Haryana, Lal Chand v. Union of India, A.P. Housing Board v. K. Manohar Reddy, Special Land Acquisition Officer v. M.K. Rafiq Saheb, and Chandrashekar v. Land Acquisition Officer.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, when evidence supports a market-value finding greater than the award, the award must reflect the value the court found.
